title: Beyond Pixel Histories: World Models with Persistent 3D State
claim: A generative loop factors into staged modules that each pass latent state forward, grounding output in an explicit persistent intermediate representation.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right four-stage chain, feedback loop on top, renders below
description: A single wide flow diagram runs left to right through four colored blocks: a green World Denoiser, a red Camera Model, a gray World Projection and a blue Pixel Denoiser. Small icons show the data passed between blocks: a controller for actions, a green voxel cube for the world latent, a red camera, a green square for the projected stack and a blue square for pixel latents. Equals signs and arrows link each block to its output. Bracketed input sets with plus signs feed each denoiser from above. A thick black line with a circular-arrows symbol closes the autoregressive loop along the top. Below each stage is a Minecraft-style render: an isometric voxel world, the same world with a red camera frustum, and green and blue frustums showing rendered frames. A yellow avatar marks the agent. The eye goes first to the colored blocks.
caption: Initialized with a single pixel frame, PERSIST evolves in an autoregressive loop in response to user actions \includegraphics[height=1.5ex]{figs/action.png}. We first denoise the 3D environment centred on the agent in the form of a latent world-frame \includegraphics[height=1.85ex]{figs/voxels.png}. Next, camera parameters \includegraphics[height=1.5ex]{figs/camera.png} are predicted with a feed-forward transformer. We then project the world to the camera plane to form a depth-ordered stack of world latents \includegraphics[height=1.5ex]{figs/voxel_frame.png}. Finally, pixel latents \includegraphics[height=1.5ex]{figs/pixel.png} are denoised, using pixel-aligned 3D information from the world latents stack \includegraphics[height=1.5ex]{figs/voxel_frame.png} as guidance.
abstract: Interactive world models continually generate video by responding to a user's actions, enabling open-ended generation capabilities. However, existing models typically lack a 3D representation of the environment, meaning 3D consistency must be implicitly learned from data, and spatial memory is restricted to limited temporal context windows. This results in an unrealistic user experience and presents significant obstacles to downstream tasks such as training agents. To address this, we present PERSIST, a new paradigm of world model which simulates the evolution of a latent 3D scene: environment, camera, and renderer. This allows us to synthesise new frames with persistent spatial memory and consistent geometry. Both quantitative metrics and a qualitative user study show substantial improvements in spatial memory, 3D consistency, and long-horizon stability over existing methods, enabling coherent, evolving 3D worlds. We further demonstrate novel capabilities, including synthesising diverse 3D environments from a single image, as well as enabling fine-grained, geometry-aware control over generated experiences by supporting environment editing and specification directly in 3D space. Project page: https://francelico.github.io/persist.github.io
